item.content:encoded:
This isn't a story, really. It's more an excuse to make someone imagine how unpleasant it would be to be stuck in a concrete lump and force-fed raw meat, which puts this into kind of the same territory as a torture porn genre movie. And in that function, I don't find myself moved a whole lot, since as a reader I'm just sort of dropped into this scene without context and for no apparent narrative purpose.

I'm also generally uninterested when people use articles as a vehicle to dump their personal interpretations of what things are, without any real structure around it beyond "hey, here's what I think this is." I don't find a whole lot of threads in the original 173 article that point to this; it's never mentioned to be shitting or eating, which you would think would be easily observable in its documentation if that's what were going on. So it doesn't really have any means of narrative support outside of itself.

They are, physically. If you really wanted to, if you could destroy the statue, the man would be alive. The cement around him, though, is so tight he literally cannot move his limbs; he's been in a stiff stress position ever since he was a child. His body has literally conformed to fit.

They could free him, but it would destroy 173. Even if they knew; it's a question of what the foundation determines to be of importance.

item.title: Hint
item.content:encoded:
The Endosymbiotic theory of evolution in Biology explains why chloroplasts and mitochondria have such similar structures to modern E-coli and bacteria cells. The theory states that somewhere along our evolutionary line, bacteria entered into early cells and found it was more beneficial to mooch off of the cell then kill it. Overtime they developed a mutually beneficial relationship, and then fused to become one creature (the mitochondria provides energy to the cell, and the cell provides everything else to the mitochondria). Neither can live on their own as they once were.

173 came into existence around a child, who was originally modified accordingly by an unknown party to live in it. As the child grew inside the cement, his body became contorted to fit; he knows nothing but this existence. Waste flows out through a tube, and he eats the food that 173 provides for him in exchange for…

…:)

A lot of the story isn't told. Maybe it's been lost to time. Maybe not. Maybe it was just a parent looking for the safest way of life for their child.

item.content:encoded:
This is super gross, which I absolutely don't have a problem with in Foundationverse canon, but it's setting up a lot of irregular/never-before-seen types of events relating to 173's nature and not giving any ounce of explanation or backstory1 for said events. This leaves me with two results after reading: squicked out, and confused about setting and context. I find myself wondering why and how 173 could be a human in a cask, and wondering about the logistics and function too; how and why does it snap necks when it's stuck like this? If people are feeding it… dead bodies, I inferred (or is it just chunks of random meat and body parts?) then why does it do what it does? If this is the only way the guy inside can live, then one would infer that — since feeding him isn't in the article's containment procedures — he would be dead in containment. Unless we're supposed to infer that he's eating the people he kills when he snaps necks, but again, that doesn't happen in containment enough for him to still be animate/alive.

The infamous blood and shit on the floor of the containment chamber was explained well and was worth its weight in body horror, but the rest doesn't quite make sense to me. I'm left wondering about additional context and backstory, but in a 'this feels incomplete in relation to how much new material it suggests' rather than a 'whoa, that was ominous' way. It's promising, but no-vote for the above reasons.

Footnotes
1. Edit: There is some backstory (the 'cave') but not enough, for the reasons mentioned later down in this paragraph. Although I think the 'cave' means his cask around his body rather than an actual cave in which he's held, right? Apologies if I'm missing something with this specific aspect.
